subject: SDLC compiled proof request — CI guardrails & secrets controls
messages:
From: Tom LaSalle <tom.lasalle@fintrustsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDLC artefacts for SIG assessment — initial ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our SIG assessor asked for a compact set of SDLC artefacts focused on code review enforcement, CI gate evidence, secrets handling, and change-authority records so they can complete the control mapping.

Could you provide: a short runbook or summary that describes the enforcement points (PR gating, merge approvals), a snapshot of CI pipeline runs for the last 30 days that show gating behavior, a current secrets rotation matrix (owners & rotation cadence), and the change-approval log for the period Apr–Jun 2028? We only need a concise packet (<= 10 files).

If you have the files hosted (Drive link) that works; otherwise attachments are fine. Goal is to get the assessor what they need by EOD Tuesday (2028-07-02).

Appreciate it — Tom
Security, FinTrust Systems
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom LaSalle <tom.lasalle@fintrustsys.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SDLC artefacts for SIG assessment — initial ask

Team — forwarding FinTrust's request. They want a tight packet focused on four items: PR gating/code review enforcement, CI gate evidence, secrets rotation matrix, and change approval logs (Apr–Jun). Target delivery: EOD Tue 7/2.

Quick asks:
- Irene: can you pull the PR gating+merge approval policy and a one-page runbook describing how we enforce it (CLA/required reviewers, automated checks)?
- Marissa: can you produce CI snapshots (pipeline runs with gate pass/fail and timestamps) for 2028-05-01 through 2028-06-30 and a short note about how ephemeral credentials are issued during builds? Zip is fine.
- Karthik: please export the secrets rotation matrix and confirm rotation cadence and KMS/HSM controls (owner, cadence, last rotation). Also include the change-approval log (CSV) that shows approvals for Apr–Jun.

Let's keep the packet concise. If you need me to redact anything before sending, loop me in.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom LaSalle <tom.lasalle@fintrustsys.com>
Date: 2028-06-29T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SDLC artefacts for SIG assessment — initial ask

Sofia / team — attaching the one-page PR gating summary (sdlc_runbook_v3.pdf) and a short FAQ that clarifies when auto-merge is allowed. Highlights: required approval from two reviewers (one from SEC/Platform), automated checks include Lint, SAST scan, and test coverage threshold (75%). Merge blocks if any of the checks fail.

Attachment stubs:
- sdlc_runbook_v3.pdf (1 page summary + diagram)

Also noted an outstanding question from the assessor about delegated approvers for emergency patches — I've flagged that for Marissa to include in the change log export.

Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom LaSalle <tom.lasalle@fintrustsys.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SDLC artefacts for SIG assessment — initial ask

Folks — attached CI snapshots and change log extract. Notes:
- ci_pipeline_snapshot_202806.zip (contains 30 pipeline run manifests for services in the serving runtime and orchestration layer; each manifest includes gate pass/fail and artifact hashes)
- change-approvals-log.csv (exported from Jira approvals with approver IDs, timestamp, justification field; includes emergency patch flag)

A few clarifications for the assessor: ephemeral build credentials are minted via our ephemeral vault service (short TTL, scoping per pipeline job). The manifest in the zip includes an example TTL trace for one build.

Let me know if we should redact any commit hashes or if they need full pipeline logs — this package is intentionally trimmed to pass/fail and artifact references.

Marissa Cole
Senior Release Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom LaSalle <tom.lasalle@fintrustsys.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC compiled proof request — CI guardrails & secrets controls

Tom / Sofia — attaching the secrets rotation matrix and a small CSV excerpt of rotation events for Apr–Jun 2028.

Attachment stubs:
- secrets_rotation_matrix.xlsx (owners, rotation cadence, KMS key alias, last rotation date)
- change-approvals-log.csv (sent earlier by Marissa; reattached here for completeness)

Key points: all service credentials used in production rotate at least every 90 days; KMS keys have annual rotation with HSM-backed key material. Rotations are logged to our audit pipeline and immutable logs are retained for 2 years.

Sofia — happy to redact any entries for external delivery (e.g., replace internal usernames with role tokens) if required.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Platform | Redwood Inference

> Thanks everyone — this looks good. We'll review and reach back if we need anything else.
>
> Tom
